oi.text: Non–operating income decreased by $1,023,000 compared to the same period last year, as further detailed in Note 6 to our interim condensed consolidated financial statements. The primary driver of the decrease in non-operating income are losses at the multi-family development in Franklin, Tennessee. The multi-family development is opening the apartment buildings in phases and we are currently in the lease-up phase. We have incurred losses of $743,000 during the third quarter of 2026 related to this development.

opex.text: Other operating expenses increased $2,857,000, or 3.0%, to $99,461,000 for the 2026 period compared to $96,604,000 for the 2025 period. Other operating expenses as a percentage of net operating revenues was 24.4% and 25.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $5,193,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

costs.heading: Total costs and expenses
costs.text:
Total costs and expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period of 2025 increased $15,056,000, or 4.3% to $367,339,000 from $352,283,000.

Salaries, wages, and benefits increased $18,761,000, or 8.0%, to $251,937,000 from $233,176,000. Salaries, wages, and benefits as a percentage of net operating revenues was 61.8% compared to 60.9% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $10,901,000 in salaries, wages, and benefits for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Other operating expenses increased $2,857,000, or 3.0%, to $99,461,000 for the 2026 period compared to $96,604,000 for the 2025 period. Other operating expenses as a percentage of net operating revenues was 24.4% and 25.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $5,193,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Facility rent expense decreased $9,980,000 for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the prior year period. The rent decrease is due from the July 1, 2026 acquisition of the thirty-five real estate assets from NHI.

other_opex.text: Other operating expenses increased $2,857,000, or 3.0%, to $99,461,000 for the 2026 period compared to $96,604,000 for the 2025 period. Other operating expenses as a percentage of net operating revenues was 24.4% and 25.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $5,193,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

nonint.text: Other operating expenses increased $2,857,000, or 3.0%, to $99,461,000 for the 2026 period compared to $96,604,000 for the 2025 period. Other operating expenses as a percentage of net operating revenues was 24.4% and 25.2% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $5,193,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

nonop.heading: Other income
nonop.text: Non–operating income decreased by $1,023,000 compared to the same period last year, as further detailed in Note 6 to our interim condensed consolidated financial statements. The primary driver of the decrease in non-operating income are losses at the multi-family development in Franklin, Tennessee. The multi-family development is opening the apartment buildings in phases and we are currently in the lease-up phase. We have incurred losses of $743,000 during the third quarter of 2026 related to this development.

tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text: The income tax provision for the three months ended September 30, 2026 is $5,498,000 (an effective income tax rate of 27.9%).

net.text: The increase in adjusted net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by the June 1, 2026 acquisition of the five skilled nursing facilities and the July 1, 2026 acquisition of the real estate of thirty-two skilled nursing facilities and three independent living facilities from NHI.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $204,953,000 as compared to $168,271,000 in the same period last year. Cash provided by operating activities consisted of net income of $90,821,000 and adjustments for non–cash items of $50,305,000. There was cash provided by working capital in the amount of $64,038,000 and $62,731,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Included in the adjustments for non-cash items are depreciation expense, equity in earnings of unconsolidated investments, unrealized gains on our marketable equity securities, gain on sale of property and equipment, deferred taxes, and stock compensation.

da.text: Included in the adjustments for non-cash items are depreciation expense, equity in earnings of unconsolidated investments, unrealized gains on our marketable equity securities, gain on sale of property and equipment, deferred taxes, and stock compensation.

capex.text: Included in the adjustments for non-cash items are depreciation expense, equity in earnings of unconsolidated investments, unrealized gains on our marketable equity securities, gain on sale of property and equipment, deferred taxes, and stock compensation.

net sales.heading: Net operating revenues
net sales.text:
Net patient revenues increased $26,457,000, or 7.1%, compared to the same period last year.

The total census at owned and leased skilled nursing facilities for the quarter averaged 90.4%, compared to an average of 90.0% for the same quarter a year ago. Overall, the composite skilled nursing facility per diem increased 5.0% compared to the same quarter a year ago. Our Medicare and Managed Care per diem rates increased 1.7% and 20.1%, respectively, compared to the same quarter a year ago. Medicaid and private pay per diem rates increased 2.3% and 5.5%, respectively, compared to the same quarter a year ago. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, $0 and $1,838,000 have been included in our net patient revenues for supplemental Medicaid payments from the state of Tennessee.

The operations of the five skilled nursing facilities that we acquired from National attributed to an increase of $19,278,000 in net patient revenues for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

Other revenues decreased $1,147,000, or 9.8%, compared to the same quarter last year, as further detailed in Note 5 to our interim condensed consolidated financial statements.

intro.text: As of August 1, 2026, NHC affiliates operate for themselves and third parties 80 skilled nursing facilities with 10,323 beds. NHC affiliates also operate 26 assisted living communities with 1,413 units, nine independent living communities with 775 units, three behavioral health hospitals, 34 homecare agencies, and 33 hospice agencies. NHC’s other services include Alzheimer’s and memory care units, pharmacy services, a rehabilitation services company, and providing management and accounting services to third party post-acute operators. Other information about the company can be found on our web site at www.nhccare.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In fiscal year 2025, 96.8% of our net operating revenues were derived from such health care services.
In fiscal year 2025, 3.2% of our net operating revenues were derived from such sources.
We depend on reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid and other third – party payors, and reimbursement rates from such payors may be reduced.
Our ability to satisfy these requirements will depend upon our ability to attract and retain qualified nurses, certified nurses' assistants, and other staff.
In addition, our ability to expand operations in a state depends on our ability to obtain necessary state licenses to operate and, where required, certificate of need approval.
We depend on the proper function and availability of our information systems.
Our primary sources of cash include revenues from the operations of our healthcare operations, management and accounting services, rental income, and investment income.
Our ability to meet our long–term contractual obligations and to finance our operating requirements, growth and development plans will depend upon our future performance.
